title: Two-Way Prepositions with Movement
summary: Using location and direction with verbs like legen, stellen, hängen, and fahren.
whyItMatters: Two-way prepositions show whether something is located somewhere or moves toward a destination.

mentalModel.title: Ask where or where to
mentalModel.content: Wo describes location and normally takes dative; wohin describes destination and takes accusative.

mentalModel.title: Meaning controls case
mentalModel.content: Movement alone is not enough; the key question is whether a boundary or destination is being entered.

ruleBlocks.title: Learn the preposition set
ruleBlocks.content: An, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, and zwischen can take dative or accusative.

ruleBlocks.title: Use position-action pairs
ruleBlocks.content: Compare stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, sitzen/setzen, and hängen as position or placement.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose case from the spatial role
ruleBlocks.content: Use in der Stadt for location and in die Stadt for destination.

tables.title: Location and Direction
rows: Der Bus steht vor dem Bahnhof.
Der Bus fährt vor den Bahnhof.
Das Rad hängt an der Wand.
Ich hänge das Rad an die Wand.

examples.en: We are waiting at the stop.

examples.de: Stell den Koffer neben die Tür.
examples.en: Put the suitcase next to the door.

examples.de: Die Fahrkarten liegen auf dem Tisch.
examples.en: The tickets are lying on the table.

commonMistakes.reason: Sein describes location, so dative is required.

commonMistakes.wrong: Choose accusative for every movement verb.
commonMistakes.correct: Ask whether the phrase expresses a destination or merely movement at a location.

comparisons.summary: City travel provides destinations, locations, and transport contexts.
Route instructions rely on accurate spatial phrases.
